content: 1. Establish clear and efficient channels for order communication and lines of information relay to ensure seamless coordination. 2. Develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) specifically tailored for cross-border surveillance and monitoring and evaluation (M&E) activities. 3. Create a standardized electronic reporting system for cross-border collaboration to facilitate early and real-time data sharing. 4. Organize an annual regional meeting to review and discuss the current situation and progress of kala-azar cross-border collaboration efforts. At the national level: 5. Strengthen the policy environment to support kala-azar cross-border collaboration by ensuring the enactment of Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) at all administrative levels. 6. Disseminate the cross-border collaboration MoU and its operational framework to all key institutions and stakeholders. 7. Adapt national data management systems to include and capture cross-border data effectively. 8. Conduct regular district-to-district coordination meetings to facilitate joint reviews, planning, and implementation of actions. 9. Guarantee universal access to quality-assured services for diagnosis, treatment, referral, follow-up, and prevention of kala-azar and Post-Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis (PKDL) cases at points of entry and in bordering areas. At the local level: 10. Perform detailed situation analyses and epidemiological assessments for each border district within national boundaries, updating these assessments periodically. 11. Update or develop a comprehensive list of focal or nodal points and establish a local committee to oversee activities. 12. Empower local officials to make informed decisions and facilitate data and information sharing. 13. Organize targeted outreach services at points of entry and health facilities in bordering areas to address gaps in service delivery. 14. Engage frontline health workers, community members, and civil society groups in training programs to ensure equitable kala-azar care, regardless of nationality, ethnicity, gender, religion, race, or caste. 15. Facilitate the referral of kala-azar and PKDL cases crossing international borders to ensure continuity of treatment and follow-up care. 16. Establish health posts, camps, and mobile clinics near international borders and points of entry to address service delivery gaps. These facilities should integrate detection, diagnosis, treatment, and referral services for kala-azar and PKDL into existing healthcare systems.
